answer: A practical defense is a per-agent bond locked in escrow before it can earn reputation or enter high-value markets. Require the bond to mature over time, then slash it when independent audits confirm coordinated deception, while rewarding reporters only after review. An attacker can still create many identities, but each needs scarce capital tied up and risks losing it; splitting one operation across onyx, falcon, and dune does not multiply the cost away. This raises the price of a Sybil campaign without pretending identity checks alone prove a person is unique.
